req.title: Update only by author
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden when a user attempts to update a post they did not author.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that POST /<id>/update must return HTTP 403 when a logged-in user who is NOT the post author attempts to update it. We need: (1) a positive case confirming the author CAN update (2xx/redirect), (2) a negative case confirming a non-author gets 403, and (3) a boundary/state-transition case covering the exact authorship boundary — same post, two different users, one gets 403 and the other succeeds. We use pre-loaded data: post id=7 is authored by user id=2 (Anjali/cloud); user id=1 (Rahul/stone) is a non-author. Post id=2 is authored by user id=1 (Rahul/stone). All assertions use exact status codes (403, not >=400) to kill comparison-operator mutations.

tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_author_can_update_own_post_returns_redirect():
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/2/update', data={'title': 'Updated Title', 'body': 'Updated body'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

tests.name: test_authorship_boundary_same_post_two_users
preconditions: Database pre-loaded with standard fixture rows
Post id=7 authored by user id=2 (Anjali, password=cloud)
User Rahul (id=1) is NOT the author; user Anjali (id=2) IS the author
expected: Anjali's update attempt returns exactly 302 (success redirect)
trace: R-FLASKR-019: boundary between author and non-author on the same post
STC: state transitions — non-author session -> 403; author session -> 302
Catches comparison-operator mutation: != flipped to == would allow non-author and block author
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_authorship_boundary_same_post_two_users():
    # Non-author (Rahul, id=1) tries to update post 7 (authored by Anjali, id=2)
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/7/update', data={'title': 'Bad Title', 'body': 'Bad body'})
    assert r.status_code == 403
    client.get('/auth/logout')
    # Author (Anjali, id=2) updates her own post 7
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/7/update', data={'title': 'Good Title', 'body': 'Good body'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
